newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly steady-lower after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly steady-lower after quiet day.

text.p: Trading was quiet amid thin volume and CBOT corn futures ended mostly steady to lower on position squaring before the long holiday weekend, traders said.
Nearby September held firm relative to other months on the posting of no deliveries Friday against the September contract. Friday was first notice day for deliveries on the September.
But corn prices were showing signs of firming near the close on local short covering, they said.
"Locals tried to break it without much success though and they covered late," a trader said.
There were few changes in fundamentals.
"It's in a narrow range. A lot of them (traders) are on the sidelines ahead of the long holiday weekend and not wanting to get involved in the market," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

U.S. Midwest weather patterns received mixed reviews with some citing bullish input from outlooks for dry weather over the near term. But bearish-minded traders cited outlooks for warm weather over the near term as enhancing crop maturity thus boosting production prospects.
Corn closed 3/4 cent per bushel lower to one cent higher, with September unchanged at $3.70-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 36,000 contracts, below the 47,042 contracts traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In the corn options pit, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 200 March $3.90 puts at 49 to 50 cents, Refco Inc bought 200 December $3.50 calls and sold 200 December $3.40 puts at 3/4 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, down from 9,645 contracts Thursday.
